title: Teaching the Harness: Student-Aware Skill Transfer for LLM Agents
why: Student-Aware Teaching (SAT) has a stronger model teach a fixed student that acts through a harness with fixed tools, context, and action budget. The teacher writes reusable skills for diagnosed failures; a skill enters the library only after it raises success on matched development tasks, and saved libraries keep gains after the teacher leaves. Skill-library learning and student-aware harness teaching.
mechanism: The teacher builds a learner model that pairs an empirical profile with hypotheses about the student's limitations, tests those hypotheses with diagnostic probes, and writes reusable skills for the diagnosed failures. A skill is admitted to the library only after it raises success on matched development tasks.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): with Claude-Sonnet-5 teaching DeepSeek-V4-Flash, SAT reaches 86.46% task success across four primary runs, ahead of a profile-free teacher with the same framework (81.04%) and the untaught student (75.00%) in each run. Removing the analytical learner model lowers both prediction and success; under misleading learner profiles none of 48 candidate skills passes admission. When DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Gemini-3.8-Flash exchange libraries, each performs better with its own. Saved libraries keep average gains of up to 11.1 points after the teacher leaves.

title: Veritas: A Verifier Generation Harness for Agent Tasks
why: Veritas is a harness that automatically generates verifiers for agent tasks, which the abstract treats as the bottleneck of a self-improving system. It adds an evidence header, a library of unstated domain rules, and authoring principles partly refined by a self-improvement loop. Automatic / co-refined evaluators for self-improving agents.
mechanism: Unlike a general-purpose agent harness, Veritas generates verifiers with three added mechanisms: an evidence header stating what the verifier will observe, a library of domain rules that tasks leave unstated, and authoring principles that are partly refined by a self-improvement loop.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): evaluated on six benchmarks — four scored by execution, whose official verifiers were first certified, and two that compare pairs of responses. With the model fixed, Veritas-generated verifiers agree better with the official verdicts than those of seven other harnesses on all four execution-scored benchmarks, and are at or near the best on the two pairwise benchmarks. They also agree better than the vendor's own harness for two of three other model families. The mechanisms improve 9 of 12 harness-benchmark pairs scored by execution across three harnesses.

title: Toward Autonomous RTL and Synthesis Optimization: Benchmarking and Self-Improving Agents
why: Invited paper on autonomous RTL and synthesis optimization that pairs open-ended / reference-based benchmarks with Dr. RTL, a multi-agent framework that rewrites RTL under implementation-level evaluation and continuously improves through reusable optimization skills. Also explores agent-driven synthesis script tuning and discovery of executable synthesis algorithms.
mechanism: Dr. RTL automates critical-path analysis, RTL rewriting, and implementation-level evaluation, and continuously improves by retaining reusable optimization skills. The paper also discusses agent-driven synthesis script tuning and the discovery of executable synthesis algorithms across intermediate representations, technology-independent optimization, and technology mapping.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): evaluated on 20 real-world RTL designs, Dr. RTL achieves average WNS/TNS improvements of 21%/17% with a 6% area reduction over commercial synthesis. The paper also discusses reference-based and open-ended RTL optimization benchmarks under realistic EDA workflows.

title: A Cross-Scenario Survey and Analysis of Self-Evolving Multimodal Agents
why: Survey and cross-scenario analysis of self-evolving multimodal agents. It formalizes four criteria plus a self-reference differentia, and uses the experience-generation / feedback-acquisition / update-consolidation loop to compare mechanisms across multimodal reasoning, generation, GUI and Web navigation, and embodied manipulation, including which mechanisms transfer or are blocked. In-scope survey/audit of self-improving agents.
mechanism: Analytical framework rather than a new system: positions scenarios along ceilings on rollout count and feedback fidelity; recasts each self-improvement mechanism as a trade-off that raises a scarce factor by presupposing a task-structural resource (such as output equivalence or checkable outcomes); and judges mechanisms portable, conditional, blocked, or redundant across scenarios.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): comparative analysis rather than a new empirical leaderboard. Comparing self-evolving with fixed loops within each scenario is used to separate scenario-imposed limits from those inherent in the self-evolving design. The paper identifies matched-budget measurements that could overturn still-untested portability verdicts. Comment: 44 pages, 15 tables, 4 figures.

title: Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents
why: WikiTrace is an evidence-linked memory that distills past-task trajectories into lessons and keeps each lesson linked to a success/failure summary and the raw trajectory, so an agent can check or correct a lesson before acting. It targets memory-induced degradation in agents that improve from experience. Also listed on Hugging Face daily papers for 2026-11-11.
mechanism: Each lesson is stored as a concise insight linked to a summary of why its trajectory succeeded or failed and to the raw trajectory. On a new task the agent starts from all insights and, when one lacks details, conflicts with another, or comes from a failed task, descends through those links with terminal tools to fill in missing details or correct the insight before acting.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): on five agentic benchmarks, WikiTrace consistently outperforms existing memory approaches and a baseline given the same insights alone, while also reducing memory-induced degradation. Exact numeric margins are not stated in the abstract. Code: https://github.com/yukyeongleee/wikitrace.

title: When Should Agents Remember? Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution for LLM Agents
why: Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution (FGSE) treats experience-derived lessons as structured hypotheses and admits them into persistent agent state only after a temporary trial and tests on target-transfer, falsification, and archived-regression probes (commit, refine, or reject). Admission control for self-evolving memory / playbook updates.
mechanism: Each candidate lesson is a structured hypothesis with an explicit precondition, behavior change, expected effect, and verifier. FGSE applies the hypothesis only in a temporary state, tests it on target-transfer, falsification, and archived-regression probes, and then commits, refines, or rejects it according to measured gain and risk.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): across web, app, tool-use, and long-term memory benchmarks, FGSE reports a 39.8 WebArena success rate, 78.8 AppWorld average completion, and 0.724/0.487 Pass^1 on τ-Retail/τ-Airline, while reducing falsification failures to 5.0%, regression damage to 1.3%, and harmful committed updates to 3.6%.

title: Program-Aided Patchable Skill Evolution
why: PASE iteratively evolves agent skills by associating them with executable programs, so procedural logic can be patched from trajectory-derived experience and downstream task feedback without repeatedly rewriting natural-language skill documents. Program-aided, patchable skill-library evolution.
mechanism: Skills are paired with editable programs that hold reusable procedural logic. Trajectory-derived experience and downstream task feedback are used to make targeted updates to those executable components, reducing the need to repeatedly revise natural-language skill documents.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): across diverse models and benchmarks, PASE consistently outperforms all baselines, by achieving over 2.8% improvements. title: The RSI Tax: When Recursive Self-Improvement Is Not Worth the Cost
why: Cost audit of recursive self-improvement on continual task streams. It defines the RSI Tax as the token cost of the self-improvement process, evaluates Meta-Harness, EvoSkill, and RRSI against a bounded-note baseline, and decomposes verification, exploration, and writing costs plus later use of the written artifacts. In-scope negative-result / audit of harness-level RSI.
mechanism: Tasks on a continual stream are scored before their feedback is used for subsequent updates. The RSI Tax (token cost of the self-improvement process) is counted alongside task-execution costs. The tax is decomposed into verification, exploration, and writing costs, and later use of the associated state or artifact is tracked.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): across six methods and two language models, a bounded-note baseline matches or exceeds the observed accuracy of Meta-Harness, EvoSkill, and RRSI, with mean total-token savings of 65.6-71.0%. For those three RSI methods, verification accounts for 74.8-93.6% of the aggregate RSI Tax. A substantial share of the tax is associated with states or artifacts that are not used later in the evaluated streams.

title: Continual-ARC: Measuring Skill Acquisition over a Working Lifetime
why: Continual-ARC is a lifelong stream built from the three ARC-AGI editions that scores memory-based agent harnesses and weight-based learners on the same returning-task schedule, including persistence in the harness and post-stream memorization and generalization tests. Benchmark and audit of harness-based skill acquisition versus weight-based continual learning.
mechanism: The same tasks return after dormant gaps with fresh instances, while new tasks keep arriving. On each instance the learner may pay for demonstrations, submit answers, or act inside the harness, with paid retries; the instance score is the share of this feedback budget consumed. After the stream the learner is frozen and tested on fresh instances of seen tasks (memorization) and on unseen tasks (generalization).
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): an agent harness with frozen weights, with and without persistence, was run on Qwen3.5-9B and GLM-5.3 Flash and compared with two prompting floors, a program-induction method, and Qwen3.5-9B weights trained to imitate GLM-5.3 Flash. Persistence in the harness generally does not improve memorization unless provided with explicit expert guidance. Most harness-based methods still learn less than a floor that simply caches each task's demonstrations. No harness-based method gains on unseen tasks, whereas weight-based learning shows substantial gains. Code: https://github.com/unifyai/continual-arc.

title: NCP: Verifier-Guided Optimization of Weight-Space Control Policies
why: The Neural Control Plane (NCP) synthesizes, verifies, and versions temporary weight-space intervention rules while restoring base-model parameters after each request. The retained optimization state is a versioned table of admitted policies plus an archive of evaluated candidates, not a lasting weight update. Verifier-guided recursive self-improvement at the control-policy / harness level.
mechanism: NCP separates a pretrained model's inference data plane from a control policy that selects temporary parameter interventions. It supplies telemetry, candidate synthesis, admission criteria, priorities, and rule lifetime management; W-ISA supplies transactional execution and parameter restoration. The optimization state consists of active rules and an archive of evaluated candidates, while base-model parameters are restored after each request.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): in a local SmolLM-135M-Instruct experiment, NCP generated three candidates from development telemetry and evaluated them on separate task examples and a 4,095-target WikiText-2 slice. One projection reduced validation token repetition from 0.4133 to 0.2191, with a perplexity change of -0.0574%. All candidates produced zero newly correct exact answers, so the configured admission gate archived all three and retained the original active policy. Fresh-process repetition and saved-table resumption reproduced the measured outcomes.
